description.value: The study examined habenula resting-state functional connectivity in autistic and neurotypical individuals, group differences, developmental variability, and associations with autism-related phenotypic measures.

spans.text: Habenula alterations in resting state functional connectivity among autistic individuals

design.value: A multisite, cross-sectional resting-state functional MRI study using ABIDE I and II data, comparing autistic spectrum disorder and neurotypical groups and testing age-related and phenotypic associations.

spans.text: The combined ABIDE dataset consisted of neuroimaging data, as well as, demographic and phenotypic information from approximately 2,000 participants across 24 international sites.

The resulting z-transformed (Fisher r-to-z transformation) correlation maps were entered into group-level regression models with diagnosis (ASD, NT) as a categorical factor and age as a continuous factor, controlling for sex and scanning site using AFNI’s 3dLMEr
Participants for the current study were selected from the large-scale, multisite ABIDE I and II datasets.
Further information regarding the ABIDE data collection can be found at http://fcon_1000.projects.nitrc.org/indi/abide/abide_I.html .
Resting state, functional, and structural MRI data were acquired across the 24 scanning sites using 3T MRI scanners.
